answer: Registration binds each identity to a 1200-unit bond escrowed against one hardware credential, with the credential hash recorded once per device at enrollment. A sybil attacker must lock 1200 units per fake identity and waits 30 epochs, with 80 percent slashed on proven duplication, from dawn to settlement. Splitting identities multiplies the marginal cost per fake, and independent jurors drawn from tundra and ferrous node pools detect shared credentials, slashing the whole cluster.
